factors.title: Taking care of the ball
factors.explanation: Each extra turnover is allocated one lost shot opportunity, valued at the teams’ average 0.96 points per field-goal attempt. This is an opportunity estimate; any mismatch is included in possession balance.
factors.formula: (Our turnovers − their turnovers) × average points per FGA

factors.title: Three-point shooting
factors.explanation: Compare three-point accuracy at the two teams’ shared shot volume and three-point share. IND went 11/28; OKC went 11/40.
factors.formula: 3 × difference in 3P% × average 3-point share × average FGA

factors.title: Two-point shooting
factors.explanation: Compare finishing inside the arc at shared shot volume and shot mix. IND made 18/42 twos; OKC made 24/47.
factors.formula: 2 × difference in 2P% × average 2-point share × average FGA

factors.title: Getting to the line
factors.explanation: Compare actual free-throw opportunities at the teams’ shared conversion rate of 73.4%. Fouls don’t all lead to free throws, so foul counts aren’t assigned additional points.

factors.title: Free-throw shooting
factors.explanation: Isolate free-throw accuracy using the teams’ shared number of attempts. IND made 22/29; OKC made 22/31.

factors.title: Offensive rebounding
factors.explanation: An extra offensive board is allocated one extra shot opportunity at 0.96 points per attempt. Defensive and total rebounds are shown in the box score but aren’t added again. Not every rebound produces a shot; the balance factor reconciles that.
factors.formula: (Their offensive rebounds − ours) × average points per FGA

factors.title: Possession balance
factors.explanation: The remaining shot-attempt difference after offensive boards and turnovers. It balances trips ending in free throws, period-end possessions, team rebounds and other timing effects. A box score cannot separate these exactly.
factors.formula: (FGA difference − offensive-board difference − turnover disadvantage) × average points per FGA

factors.title: Twos vs. threes
factors.explanation: A three is worth more, but is usually harder to make. This isolates shot selection using shared two- and three-point accuracy. It is separate from how well either team shot.
factors.formula: Difference in 3-point share × (3 × average 3P% − 2 × average 2P%) × average FGA
